# shadow/jsx-no-unsafe-inner-html

Disallow `innerHTML` (and similar HTML sinks) with values that are not literals.

`recommended` `has suggestions`

## Why

`innerHTML` parses a string as markup. With anything but a constant, the string can carry `<script>`-like payloads (`<img onerror=...>`) and becomes a cross-site scripting hole. Render with JSX, or pass the value through a sanitizer that this rule is told about (`allowedSanitizers`).

## Incorrect

```tsx
<div innerHTML={comment().html} />
```

```tsx
el.innerHTML = `<b>${name}</b>`;
```

```tsx
<div dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: html }} />
```

```tsx
el.insertAdjacentHTML('beforeend', html);
```

## Correct

```tsx
<div innerHTML="<b>static</b>" />
```

```tsx
<div innerHTML={DOMPurify.sanitize(comment().html)} />
```

```tsx
<div>{comment().text}</div>
```

## Options

```json
[
  {
    "type": "object",
    "properties": {
      "allowedSanitizers": {
        "type": "array",
        "items": {
          "type": "string"
        }
      }
    },
    "additionalProperties": false
  }
]
```

Defaults: `[{"allowedSanitizers":["sanitize","sanitizeHtml","DOMPurify.sanitize","trusted","trustedHtml"]}]`

## Suggestions

For `dangerouslySetInnerHTML={{ __html: value }}` the suggestion replaces the attribute with `innerHTML={value}`, which is then checked like any other value. It is withheld when the attribute value is not an object literal with an `__html` property.

## Disabling

Disable one line with `// eslint-disable-next-line shadow/jsx-no-unsafe-inner-html`, a block with `/* eslint-disable shadow/jsx-no-unsafe-inner-html */` and `/* eslint-enable shadow/jsx-no-unsafe-inner-html */`, or a whole file with the block form at its top. Disable it only when the value is trusted HTML the rule cannot recognize, such as markup produced by your own build; for an unlisted sanitizer, add it to `allowedSanitizers` instead.

## Notes

- Option `allowedSanitizers` (default `sanitize`, `sanitizeHtml`, `DOMPurify.sanitize`, `trusted`, `trustedHtml`) lists calls whose result is trusted. Entries are exact dotted names.
- `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` (React) is always reported; the suggestion converts it to `innerHTML`, which is then checked like any other value.
- `srcdoc` of an `<iframe>` (and `prop:srcdoc`, and `.srcdoc` assignments) is checked like `innerHTML`: the browser parses it as a whole HTML document.
- A sanitizer call may be indirect, `(0, DOMPurify.sanitize)(html)`. The name `DOMPurify` is trusted only when it is the global (also one the configuration declares, or an ambient `declare const DOMPurify`) or comes from an import, `import()` or `require`; a local object or parameter named `DOMPurify` is not the library.
- Also checked: `.innerHTML` / `.outerHTML` assignments, `insertAdjacentHTML`, `createContextualFragment`, `document.write`, and the `innerHTML` / `outerHTML` / `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` keys of an object literal spread onto an element.

## Messages

- `unsafeAttribute`: `{{attr}}` is set from a value that is not a literal, so markup in it is executed. Render with JSX or sanitize the value (allowed: {{sanitizers}}).
- `unsafeAssignment`: `.{{property}}` is assigned a value that is not a literal. Use DOM nodes or sanitize the value (allowed: {{sanitizers}}).
- `unsafeSink`: `{{method}}()` parses its argument as HTML. Pass a literal or a sanitized value (allowed: {{sanitizers}}).
- `reactApi`: `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` is React's API. Use `innerHTML` with a literal or sanitized value (allowed: {{sanitizers}}).
- `useInnerHtml`: Replace `dangerouslySetInnerHTML` with `innerHTML` and the `__html` value.
